NB: system, json, strings, sequtils and regex are statically linked (lang/lowlibs). Every other stdlib (yaml, http, cli, config, browser, toml, uuid, dotenv, csv, bson, colors, qr, nanoid, llm, httpclient, xml, feed, ical, css, svg, markdown, strongpwd, twofa, fswatch, algos, bench) resolves at runtime through stdlibLoader (dylib shards built by stdkups tools/build_shards.nim, invoked from the GitHub workflows); importing them here would statically link their dependency chains into every dfkup process — notably powpow/net/tls (-lssl -lcrypto), which dyld then loads and initializes on every startup, even for echo 1.

Run a config file with std/config loaded automatically.

Without command, this behaves like runFile for a config source. With command, it executes the matching string from the config's commands object through the system shell and returns the captured output.

Loader calls are module-qualified (stdlib_loader.clearActiveConfig, etc.): the static stdlib bundle (lang/lowlibs/liball) provides identically-named helpers, so bare names would be ambiguous.
